basis: Brain malformations and severe developmental disability define disease; strabismus and scoliosis each affect 5/8. Dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction.
Mood disorder defined by manic or mixed episodes; no organ axis applies.
Aneurysmal dilatation of the abdominal aorta; downstream ischemic complications do not define additional organ involvement.
Oral and digital malformations define the group. Renal cystic disease and brain abnormalities vary by subtype; group-wide involvement above 30% is uncertain.
Congenital bilateral absence of the lower legs and feet is a skeletal limb malformation.
Mixed colorectal polyposis defines disease. Frequent anemia is secondary to gastrointestinal bleeding and separately diagnosed; cancer risk adds no axis.
Congenital aneurysm of the ductus arteriosus. Respiratory symptoms do not establish common direct airway damage; rupture and embolism are complications.
Inherited structural heart disease, predominantly ventricular septal defects; supplied phenotypes are confined to the cardiovascular axis.
The defining congenital abnormalities are jejunal atresia and renal agenesis or dysplasia.
Microliths in testicular seminiferous tissue are reproductive pathology; endocrine dysfunction is not established.
A vascular neoplasm composed of cavernous blood vessels arising in the colon.
Systemic intravascular microthrombosis with platelet and coagulation-factor consumption defines DIC; additional organ injury varies with severity.
Primordial skeletal dwarfism and abnormal brain development define disease; tooth agenesis affects 5/6 and enamel hypoplasia 2/6. Eyelid shape alone adds no axis.
Carcinoma originates in salivary glands, usually the parotid; salivary glands belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Sarcoma originates in the leptomeninges of the central nervous system.
Neurodevelopmental and hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction define PWS; visual impairment/strabismus and scoliosis each occur in 30-79%. Hypopigmentation adds no damage axis.
Bone tumor arising from notochordal remnants; neural compression depends on tumor location and is not established across the umbrella.
Hereditary Wilms tumor is a nephroblastoma originating in the kidney.
Congenital abducens dysinnervation causes ocular motility loss; supplied HPO reports hearing loss and vertebral fusion in 30-79%, though frequencies may reflect syndromic cases.
Primary carcinoma of the endometrium, a reproductive organ outside the 13 axes.
Congenital cleft malformation of the nose; the nasal structures fall within the pulmonary axis.
Inherited retinal cone dysfunction causes achromatopsia, photophobia and reduced visual acuity.
Pontocerebellar malformation and developmental disability define disease; arthrogryposis affects 2/6, esotropia and astigmatism each 2/6. Cerebral visual impairment is neurologic.
BCL11B combined immunodeficiency; brain malformation with disability, psoriasiform dermatitis and pulmonary artery stenosis each reported in 1/1; frequency evidence is limited.
Disrupted carbohydrate transport defines a metabolic disease group; neurologic and other organ damage depend on the specific transport disorder.
